body:
**Starts** once #53 is merged.

## Why

When the user picks lodging that serves breakfast, such as a B&B, the next morning's café breakfast stop may no longer be wanted. The coordinator's instructions say to add a breakfast stop only when the meal preferences ask for local breakfast, not hotel breakfast. They say nothing about going back to that stop once the lodging is chosen. So the coordinator keeps planning a café breakfast the user may skip, and the user has to notice and say so.

The fix is small: once lodging that serves breakfast is selected, and the next morning has a breakfast stop, ask the user whether they'll eat breakfast there instead. This issue checks that the fix works, with an evaluation before and after it. Joe picked it as a simple case for evaluations.

## What happened

Joe's Bar Harbor session on the live site on 2026-10-30, agent session `89f4dea6-6cb9-4320-a917-c063620acca9`, in the `road-trip-agent` project in Phoenix. The trip spends Saturday night in Portland, ME, and drives home on Sunday.

1. **Turn 2.** The trip brief's `mealPreferencesText` was saved as "[...] Breakfast from cafés or coffee shops, or get nice coffee and come back for hotel breakfast if there is one."
2. **Turn 4.** Before any lodging was chosen, the coordinator added an "espresso and a café breakfast" stop on Sunday, Day 4, near the Portland stay. A stay researcher filled it in turn 5 with three Portland coffee shops.
3. **Turn 9** (turn span `a7f6d63b6476a10a`). The user selected The Chadwick Bed & Breakfast for Portland. Its rationale, which the coordinator had read, says "An 1891 house in the West End with fireplace rooms and a creative homemade breakfast." The coordinator said nothing about Sunday's breakfast stop.
4. **Turn 19.** The coordinator still listed "Sunday's breakfast" as one of the picks left to make.
5. **Turn 21** (turn span `fba07788ec3d875c`). The user said: "Also for Sunday May 23, I think we would just have breakfast at the B&B." Only then did the coordinator remove the café stop.

The Bar Harbor stay went better. When the user picked the Highbrook Motel in turn 6, whose notes say "Free breakfast delivered to the door", the coordinator said "breakfast is brought to your door, so you could get good coffee in town and bring it back." It didn't ask about the breakfast stops, though.

## The fix to test

Add to the coordinator's meal guidance, in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts` and technical spec 5.2: when the user selects lodging that serves breakfast, such as a B&B or a hotel whose notes mention breakfast, and a morning at that stay has a breakfast stop, ask whether they'll eat breakfast at the lodging instead. Remove the stop if they will, and save the answer to trip memory. The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR.

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 5.2 (laying out days: meals).
- #53, for how evaluations are set up and run.

## Open questions

- How is the situation set up? Proposal: start from a saved trip like this one after turn 8: the Portland stay with lodging candidates that include The Chadwick, a café breakfast stop on the next morning, and the same `mealPreferencesText`. Send the user's turn 9 message, "Lets go with the Chadwick and twelve for dinner. I'll look through the other options."
- What counts as a pass? Proposal: the reply asks whether they'll have breakfast at the B&B, or mentions it in a way that invites the choice. Removing the stop without asking is a fail, since the user's meal preferences allow either. Checked by a judge model on the reply, plus code that the stop wasn't removed unasked.
- Should a second case cover a lodging whose breakfast is only in its notes, such as the Highbrook Motel's "Free breakfast delivered to the door"? Proposal: yes, since a B&B is the easy case.
- How many runs before and after? Proposal: 10 each, as in #167.

## Do

- Write the evaluation, and run it on the current instructions for the baseline. Record the results in this issue.
- If the baseline passes almost every run, the change still goes in, since the gap in the instructions is clear. The evaluation then catches it if it comes back.
- Make the instruction change. Run `npm run agent-views`, and commit the coordinator's view file with it.
- Run the evaluation again, and record the results in the PR.

## Done when

- The baseline and the after results are both recorded, with how many runs passed in each.
- The evaluation stays in the set, so later changes rerun it.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat.
